Republican Town Committee Electoral Cards

Local Republican Town Committee · Hudson Valley, NY · Political

< 3 Weeks
Turnaround
Palm Cards + Slate Mailer
Piece Types
Union Printed (APTC Label)
Print Type
Registered Voters

The Challenge

A Hudson Valley Republican Town Committee needed to produce and distribute palm cards and slate mailers for their full candidate roster ahead of a local election. The timeline was tight — less than three weeks from design approval to mailbox delivery — and the materials needed to be union-printed to satisfy party requirements.

Our Solution

Cornerstone produced union-printed palm cards bearing the Allied Printing Trades Council label and designed a coordinated slate mailer featuring all candidates with their positions and qualifications. We pulled a targeted voter list from the county Board of Elections data, filtered for registered party members, and processed the mailing through our presort system for maximum postage savings.

The Results

All materials were designed, printed, and mailed within the 3-week window. The union bug was prominently displayed on all pieces, satisfying party requirements. The committee reported strong voter recognition at polling locations, with many voters specifically mentioning the mailer when speaking with candidates. The committee has used Cornerstone for subsequent election cycles.

Background

Political direct mail is one of the most time-sensitive applications of print and mailing services. Candidates and committees operate on fixed election calendars with zero flexibility — Election Day does not move, early voting dates are set in stone, and absentee ballots go out on a schedule. This particular Hudson Valley Republican Town Committee needed to communicate their full candidate slate to registered party voters ahead of a local election cycle that included contested races for town board, highway superintendent, and town justice. The committee had used a different printer in prior cycles but experienced quality and timeline issues. They came to Cornerstone specifically because of our ability to produce union-printed materials with the Allied Printing Trades Council (APTC) label — a requirement for many political organizations that want to demonstrate labor solidarity and avoid criticism from opponents about using non-union shops.

Strategy & Execution

Voter List Acquisition and Processing

We obtained the committee's voter file extracted from the Ulster County Board of Elections database, filtered for registered Republican voters within the town. The raw file required significant cleaning — address standardization, CASS certification, duplicate removal, and NCOA processing to account for voters who had moved since the last registration update. The final list was presort-ready and optimized for maximum postal discounts.

Palm Card Design and Production

Palm cards (also called rack cards or push cards) are the staple of political campaigning — small, wallet-sized cards that volunteers hand out at events, door-to-door canvassing, and polling locations. We designed double-sided palm cards for each candidate featuring their photo, qualifications, key positions, and the committee's endorsement. All cards were printed on heavy 14pt card stock with the APTC union bug prominently displayed.

Slate Mailer Design

The slate mailer is a single mailpiece that presents the entire ticket — all endorsed candidates on one coordinated piece. We designed an 8.5" x 11" folded mailer with candidate photos, bios, and the committee's message. The design used consistent branding across all candidates to present a unified ticket image.

Union Printing Compliance

Every piece produced for this campaign carried the Allied Printing Trades Council label (union bug), certifying production in a union shop. This is not merely a label — it requires that the work be performed by union workers using union processes. Cornerstone is one of the few Hudson Valley printers maintaining APTC certification.

Design Approach

Political print materials follow specific conventions that differ from commercial marketing. Candidate photos need to be high-quality, approachable headshots — not corporate portraits. The color palette used the party's traditional red, white, and blue with the committee's local branding elements. Typography prioritized readability at small sizes (palm cards are read quickly while standing). The slate mailer hierarchy placed the top-of-ticket candidate (town supervisor) most prominently, with down-ballot candidates following in ballot order. Every piece included the required 'Paid for by' disclaimer and the APTC union label.

Postal Strategy

The slate mailer was sent via USPS Marketing Mail (Standard) to maximize postage savings on the voter list mailing. Marketing Mail rates for presorted flats were significantly lower than First-Class rates, and the 7-14 day delivery window was acceptable given that the mailing was timed three weeks before Election Day. Palm cards were not mailed — they were delivered to the committee for hand distribution at events and polling locations.

Key Takeaways

The 3-week turnaround from design approval to mailbox delivery required careful project management — political clients often delay design approval due to committee review processes, which compresses the production and mailing timeline. Building buffer time into the schedule is essential.

Union printing capability is a significant competitive advantage for political work. Many print shops cannot produce union-labeled materials, limiting committees' options. Cornerstone's APTC certification opens a market segment that most competitors cannot serve.

Voter file data quality varies significantly between counties and election cycles. Budget time for data cleaning and address validation — raw Board of Elections files typically have 5-10% undeliverable addresses that would waste postage if not cleaned.

Coordinated design across palm cards and the slate mailer created stronger brand recognition at the polls — voters who received the mailer recognized the same visual identity on the palm cards handed to them on Election Day.

Industry Context

Political direct mail is a distinct specialty within the broader direct mail industry. It operates under strict legal requirements (disclaimer language, spending limits, reporting), has immovable deadlines (election calendars), and often requires union printing certification. The Hudson Valley has an active local political landscape with contested races at the town, village, county, and state levels in virtually every election cycle. Cornerstone's combination of union printing capability, voter list processing experience, and rapid turnaround capacity makes it a natural partner for political organizations across the region. We handle campaigns for committees and candidates across the political spectrum.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Allied Printing Trades Council (APTC) union bug?
The APTC union bug (or union label) is a small logo printed on materials produced in a certified union print shop. It indicates that the work was performed by union workers under union conditions. Many political organizations, labor unions, and progressive campaigns require the union bug on all printed materials. Cornerstone is an APTC-certified shop and can produce union-labeled materials for any political or organizational client.

How far in advance should a political committee start planning direct mail?
Ideally, 6-8 weeks before the target delivery date. This allows time for voter list acquisition and processing (1-2 weeks), design and committee review (1-2 weeks), printing (3-5 business days), and mailing with delivery buffer (1-2 weeks). For EDDM campaigns that do not require voter lists, the timeline can be compressed to 3-4 weeks.

Can Cornerstone handle both party and candidate mailings?
Yes. We produce materials for town committees, county committees, individual candidate campaigns, and independent expenditure organizations. Each type has different legal disclaimer requirements — we are familiar with New York State Board of Elections rules and ensure all printed materials include compliant paid-for-by language.

What is the most effective format for political direct mail?
For voter contact, oversized postcards (6" x 9" or 8.5" x 11") consistently perform best because they are seen immediately without opening. For slate mailers presenting multiple candidates, a folded self-mailer allows enough space for photos, bios, and positions. Palm cards for hand distribution should be printed on heavy card stock (14pt minimum) to withstand handling at events and polling locations.
